title: Embedding adapter compatibility and graceful swap plan for new vector models
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary: We need a compatibility adapter + migration strategy that allows us to introduce higher-quality embedding models (different dimensionality and normalization) into the embeddings and reranking endpoints without breaking downstream indexes, recall characteristics, or latency SLOs. This ticket defines the engineering plan, gating metrics, migration tooling, and rollback procedure for a graceful model swap across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Problem: New candidate models offer up to +6% recall@10 and better semantic clustering but change vector dimension from 1024 -> 1280 and use L2-normalization by default. Immediate replacement would invalidate existing vector indexes, increase storage and compute, and risk regressions for customers with pinned model aliases. We must avoid painful all-at-once reindexing and provide fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes.

Goals:
- Enable model variant routing via an adapter layer that presents the same API contract to callers.
- Support mixed-dimension index strategy and on-the-fly vector transformation where feasible.
- Minimize customer-visible downtime and keep p95 latency delta < +20ms on embedding calls.
- Provide automated canary, phased traffic ramp, and clear rollback paths.
- Produce telemetry and automatic quality gates tied to offline evals and production metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter layer can serve embeddings from old and new models behind same API with explicit model_alias header
Canary ramp pipeline that increments tenant traffic in configurable steps (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with automated gating
Migration tool that can generate re-embedding jobs with sharding, rate-limiting, and resume on failure
Telemetry dashboard shows recall@10, recall@50, mean cosine drift, p95 latency, and cost per-embedding for both variants
Rollback can be triggered automatically if quality gates fail or manually via Console with < 15min rollback time
milestones: M1: Adapter prototype for dimension-agnostic API (2026-03-18)
M2: Offline evaluation harness & baseline run on eval set (2026-03-22)
M3: Canary infra + gating automation + dashboard (2026-03-28)
M4: Controlled tenant pilot + reindex tooling (2026-03-31)
telemetry_metrics: recall@10_delta: abs(delta) must be <= 1.5% for canary pass
mean_cosine_drift: monitor per-tenant drift, >0.02 triggers review
cost_per_1M_embeddings: compare delta against budget threshold
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Internal staging run on shadow traffic for 48h, full telemetry capture.
Phase 1: 1% tenant traffic across low-risk tenants (no contract SLOs) for 24h.
Phase 2: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automated gating after each step (24h per step, can be shortened if metrics stable).
Phase 3: Full cutover only after 7 days of stable 50% and zero critical regressions.
Fallback: Route tenant traffic back to previous model alias via adapter with atomic config change. Reindexing is asynchronous and optional for tenants; provide per-tenant reindex scheduler in Console.
Notes: For Dedicated and Private customers we provide a toggle in their Console and a dry-run mode that shows expected storage delta and estimated reindex time using sample throughput metrics.
risks: Index incompatibility causing silent retrieval regressions for semantic search
Increased storage and memory pressure for GPU endpoints and indexes
Unexpected latency degradation due to higher-dimensional vectors and cache misses
Edge-case downstream consumers relying on raw vector dimensionality (rare, but possible)
Operational complexity for Private customers with air-gapped upgrade cadence
notes: Trade-offs considered: full-force reindex vs. dual-index strategy (we choose dual-index + on-demand re-embed)
We will not change the public embedding shape in the API; we present a stable JSON schema and use adapter for translation
Cost mitigation: recommend quantized storage for the new model vectors where supported and provide per-tenant quota controls
